newsitem.title: FINLAND: Markka money rates off lows as rate cut hopes fade.
newsitem.headline: Markka money rates off lows as rate cut hopes fade.

text.p: Finnish money market rates and bond yields closed off session lows on Monday after the Bank of Finland said it did not intend to cut its key tender rate in the near term regrdless of the Bundesbank's actions, dealers said.
FRA rates jumped some six basis points on average following the news.
"It dampened rate cut expectations for now -- but if there is some action from Buba they will be back on the agenda," one dealer said.
Currently, the tender rate at 3.00 percent -- lowered from 3.10 percent on October 9 -- is on par with the German repo rate.
Analysts said it seemed that the Bank of Finland was set on keeping the Finnish/German short interest rate gap steady.

If the central bank were to let the tender rate remain above the German repo rate it would only bolster the attractiveness of the markka -- as the interest rate on Finnish currency deposits comes from the tender rate, they said.
"A rate gap would only increase the attractiveness of the markka," said one.
The markka rallied against the mark in heavy trading with DEM/FIM falling briefly below key support at 2.90.
But the markka slipped off its highs after the Bank of Finland said that the state will buy foreign currency direct from the markets to meet its debt financing needs.
